research_scope: Five source-free full-reference reviews: free resolution, Ext, Tor, direct-summand projectivity and Hom projectivity. No new meanings or external research.

amendments.review_rationale: Full-formulation semantic review of free resolutions, chain/cochain complexes, homology and cohomology, arbitrary-rank free/direct-summand modules and projective Hom exactness, preserving complete prior adjacency and original source version.
amendments.reason: Source-free Wave2 Pass2 typed prerequisite consolidation for homological algebra; provisional identities require later cross-definition consistency audit.

references.context: Module theory: free left R-module over a unital ring with an R-basis, equivalently a direct sum R^{(I)} of copies of R, possibly infinite rank.
references.reason: A free R-module is independent prerequisite data for a free resolution.
references.matching_note: Compare with R^(I), finite free modules, and categorical projectivity; free does not mean finite rank.

references.context: Homological algebra: augmented nonnegative chain complex of R-modules with differentials d_i:F_i→F_{i-1}, augmentation ε:F_0→M, zero composites, and an exactness condition for being a resolution.
references.reason: The chain-complex structure, augmentation, and exactness are typed mathematical prerequisites, not a mere sequence of arrows.
references.matching_note: Compare graded chain versus cochain complex and general exact augmented complex; exactness supplied separately.

references.disposition: Free implies projective under standard unital module conventions, but the definition explicitly chooses free rather than arbitrary projectives.

references.context: Homological algebra: cochain complex induced by contravariant Hom_R(−,N) on a chain complex F_•, with coboundary maps induced by precomposition with the original differentials.
references.reason: The construction distinguishes cohomological degree and reversed arrows from an ordinary chain complex.
references.matching_note: Free resolution and Hom_R module are already linked; don't treat Ext as a prior notion.

references.phrase: ith cohomology of a cochain complex
references.context: Homological algebra: ith cohomology H^i(C^•)=ker(d^i:C^i→C^{i+1})/im(d^{i−1}:C^{i−1}→C^i) for a cochain complex, with im contained in ker.
references.reason: Cohomology is a separately reusable construction on cochain complexes, not the derived Ext group itself.
references.matching_note: Keep cohomology distinct from homology of chain complexes (Tor).

references.disposition: The superscript indexes cohomology, not ordinary ring exponentiation, and no particular free resolution is preferred.

references.matching_note: Both arguments of Tor are unital modules over the commutative ring.
The grading index is a nonnegative integer.
This is the explicitly indexed free resolution of the module.
The complex is tensored termwise over the ring R.

references.context: Homological algebra: ith homology H_i(C_•)=ker(d_i:C_i→C_{i−1})/im(d_{i+1}:C_{i+1}→C_i) of a chain complex of modules.
references.reason: Homology is a general chain-complex construction used to define Tor, independent of Tor itself.
references.matching_note: Not the ith cohomology of a cochain complex.
A second reference to the very same existing free resolution already linked by 'free resolution of M'; the chain-complex structure is part of its stated meaning, not an extra missing resolution.

references.disposition: The isomorphism type's independence from the chosen free resolution is a well-definedness statement.

references.phrase: free module R^(I) on index set I
references.context: Module theory: free R-module R^{(I)} of finitely supported functions I→R, direct sum of one copy of R for each i∈I; I may be infinite.
references.reason: The characterization of projectivity permits free modules of arbitrary rank.
references.matching_note: Compare with free-module prerequisite for resolutions and finite free presentation separately.

references.context: Module theory: external direct sum P⊕Q of two R-modules, with canonical injections and projections; P is a direct summand of R^{(I)} when P⊕Q≅R^{(I)}.
references.reason: The direct-summand structure is independent of projectivity and is a separate categorical/module construction.
references.matching_note: Do not conflate external direct sum with internal sum or direct product for infinite families.

references.phrase: free module need not have finite rank
references.disposition: The characterization of arbitrary projectives allows infinite index set I, unlike finite projective modules.

references.context: Module category: covariant functor Hom_R(P,−) from R-Mod to abelian groups/modules where appropriate, sending N to Hom_R(P,N), g:N→N' to postcomposition g∘−.
references.reason: The Hom functor is a reusable structure, not merely the Hom_R(P,N) object; source/target category sizes should not be unnecessarily restricted.
references.matching_note: Contrast contravariant Hom_R(−,N) and small-category-only covariant functors.

references.context: Set theory: surjective function f:X→Y whose image is the entire stated codomain Y; for module homomorphisms this is the underlying-set surjectivity of the R-linear map, independent of linearity, free domain, or choice of basis.
references.matching_note: The structured map is surjective on underlying sets. Module linearity or topological continuity and discrete two-point codomain are additional requirements.

references.disposition: The assertion that every map P→N admits a lift P→M across every surjective M→N is the *defining equivalent projectivity criterion* of this formulation, not a pre-existing extra type of projective module.
A pair of equivalent projectivity criteria; this is not the weaker property of being finitely generated.
